name: Mountain Meadow
lede: Mountain Meadow is a vivid, blue-leaning green named for a kind of place rather than any one documented location, and it has no match anywhere in our painting archive.

sections.title: A landscape type, not a landmark
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, with no first-recorded date given [1]. ColorHub groups it among place and institution names because it names a kind of landscape, a high mountain clearing, though no single documented meadow stands behind it [1]. A related library entry, the gemstone Chrysoprase, a green chalcedony, is dated by Maerz and Paul to 1835 [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[jungle-green|Jungle Green]], 4.4 units away and darker [2]. [[caribbean-green|Caribbean Green]] sits 4.8 units out, more vivid and lighter, and [[green-crayola|Green (Crayola)]] 5.0 units out, darker [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 68, chroma 48, a saturated mid-tone green [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact green covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes a gap in this particular archive, not a claim about painting as a whole [3]. In printed English, the phrase "mountain meadow" rose fastest from the 1860s and peaked around 1930, by Google Books count across all senses of the words, so the curve tracks the landscape phrase rather than any color swatch [1].
